The Galley Supervisor will oversee all Food Services activities as directed by the Galley Manager. The main areas of concentration will be the oversight of the kitchen operations, food preparation, and inventory levels. The Supervisor will oversee the scheduling and training of employees. In the absence of the Galley Manager, the Galley Supervisor will be the Galley POC.
q: Education/Certifications: One year of related experience may be substituted for one year of education if a degree is required.
Must have a current US Driver’s License.
Current food service sanitation, food protection manager certification and safety training requirements such as ServSafe® Manager or other accredited program - IAW P5010 Chapter1 Section 2-1.2.2.D
All contractor chefs must have Certified Culinary Certification issued by the American Culinary Federation.
Prior military must be E-6 and above former Mess Management Specialist or Culinary Specialist rating if prior Navy or equivalent MOS for other service.
At least five years of foodservice experience in a military Food Services or cafeteria-style or multi-entrée operations providing complete meal services (breakfast, lunch, and dinner).
At least one year of experience as a food service manager or assistant manager. Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office products (i.e. PowerPoint, Word, Excel)
Must be computer literate and proficient in MS Office software.
Must be able to read and speak English.
r: Manage subcontractors with food preparation, food serving, cashier operations, cleanliness of the dining areas, serving lines, kitchens, temperature danger zones, dishwashing area, and storage areas IAW with PWS and SOPs. Ensure proper cooking techniques are being applied IAW standards and guidelines as established by NAVSUP P-486, NAVSUP P-7, The Armed Forces Recipe Service, NAVSUP P-476, Navy Food Service, NAVSUP P-580, Fat, Cholesterol and Calories List for General Messes, The New Professional Chef, and The Art and Science of Culinary Preparation. Maintain all equipment accountability and serviceability and turn-in and ordering of stock levels.
Manage scheduling and training for the sub-contractor workforce to ensure compliance with requirements IAW PWS
Direct and ensure that required procedures are followed.
Ensure that all employees are always in compliance with all established Safety Policies and Regulations.
Performs other duties and assignments as required.
Required to Supervise FN workforce for all Food Services requirements. Not responsible for any Supervisor Budgets.

We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Marine Inspector to join our organization in Kuwait City, Kuwait. In this role, you will play a critical part in ensuring the integrity and compliance of marine operations and infrastructure. You will conduct comprehensive inspections of marine facilities, vessels, and port operations, evaluating adherence to international maritime standards, local Kuwait regulations, and safety protocols. As a Marine Inspector, you will demonstrate exceptional analytical capabilities, decisive judgment, and a commitment to maintaining the highest standards of marine safety and operational excellence. Your work will directly impact the safety of personnel, protection of assets, and compliance with regulatory requirements.
Conduct thorough and systematic inspections of marine facilities, vessels, equipment, and port infrastructure, documenting findings with precision and clarity
Analyze operational procedures, maintenance records, and safety protocols against established maritime standards and regulatory requirements
Prepare detailed inspection reports documenting observations, non-conformances, deficiencies, and actionable recommendations for corrective measures
Evaluate compliance with international maritime standards, local Kuwait regulations, and organizational policies across all marine operations
Collaborate with vessel operators, facility managers, and project teams to address inspection findings and implement corrective actions
Monitor adherence to safety protocols and environmental regulations throughout all marine operations and maintenance activities
Identify potential risks, hazards, and safety concerns, providing expert guidance on mitigation strategies and preventive measures
Maintain comprehensive and organized documentation of all inspections, test results, certifications, and compliance records
Communicate inspection findings, recommendations, and regulatory updates to operational leadership and relevant authorities with transparency and professionalism
Conduct follow-up inspections to verify implementation of corrective actions and ensure sustained compliance
Stay current with evolving maritime regulations, industry best practices, and inspection methodologies
Support continuous improvement initiatives by identifying operational inefficiencies and recommending process enhancements
q: Minimum 8 years of professional experience in marine inspection, port operations, or maritime facility management and supervision
Demonstrated expertise in international maritime construction standards, protocols, and best practices
Advanced proficiency in marine inspection methodologies, quality assurance procedures, and specialized inspection techniques
Solid understanding of marine engineering principles, port infrastructure systems, and vessel operations
Comprehensive knowledge of safety compliance standards and environmental regulations in maritime operations
Proven ability to analyze complex operational scenarios and make decisive, independent judgments regarding compliance and safety
Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to prepare clear, professional inspection reports
Advanced attention to detail with a commitment to identifying non-conformances and ensuring thorough documentation
Proficiency with inspection software, digital documentation tools, and data management systems
Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple inspections and priorities efficiently
Proven supervisory or coordination experience in marine or port environments
Physical capability to conduct on-site inspections in various weather conditions and challenging environments
Knowledge of local Kuwait maritime regulations and familiarity with regional operational requirements
Ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams while maintaining professional independence and objectivity
Problem-solving mindset with a proactive approach to identifying and resolving operational challenges
Professional certifications in marine inspection, maritime safety, or related maritime disciplines (preferred)
x: All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
